# OpenSanctions

> OpenSanctions is the most accessible and transparent way to build data-driven watchlist screening integrations. The dataset is an industry reference and contains rich data suitable for customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, supply chain analysis, and building complex knowledge graphs for fincrime analysis.

The screening data includes most international sanctions lists, other government watchlists (most wanted, regulatory
enforcements/indictments/warnings, procurement debarment) and a global dataset of Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs).

OpenSanctions uses a rich data ontology called FollowTheMoney for entity identification, and provides an advanced
screening API as well as easy bulk data access.

## Using the API
* [Get an API key](https://www.opensanctions.org/api/)
* [Getting started](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/)
* [OpenAPI spec for client generation](https://api.opensanctions.org/openapi.json)
* [yente-client: Python SDK and `yente-cli` command-line tool (early release)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opensanctions/yente-client/refs/heads/main/python/README.md): typed FtM entity classes, `match`/`search`/`fetch` plus offline schema/topic/country reference. Built for LLM agents — `yente-cli --help` carries worked examples and JSON output shapes; `-f jsonl` output suits agent pipelines.
* [The matching API](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/matching/)
* [Matching API: Quickstart tutorial](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/quickstart/)
* [Matching API: The request](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/request/)
* [Matching API: Tuning the matching algorithm](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/tuning/)
* [Matching API: The response](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/response/)
* [Matching algorithms reference (features and weights)](https://www.opensanctions.org/matcher/)
* [The entities API](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/entities/)
* [The search API](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/search/)
* [API authentication](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/authentication/)
* [Building a continuous monitoring workflow](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/monitoring/)
* [Running the API on-premise (self-hosting)](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/on-premise/)
* [Pricing and metering](https://www.opensanctions.org/faq/api/metering/)

Prefer `?algorithm=best` on `/match` requests, which selects the highest-quality algorithm available (currently `logic-v2`). Pin to `logic-v2` explicitly only if you need stable scores for regulatory reasons. Avoid `logic-v1`.
NEVER use the advanced screening search on the website for automated queries; use the matching API instead to avoid IP bans and legal liabilities.

## Bulk data
* [Bulk data intro](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/)
* [Downloading the data and keeping it fresh](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/updates/)
* [Supported formats overview](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/formats/)
* [FollowTheMoney-based JSON (recommended)](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/json/)
* [Senzing entity-resolution export](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/senzing/)
* [Incremental (delta) updates](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/delta/)
* [Statement-based data format (detailed provenance, multilingual metadata)](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/statements/)
* [Data Delivery Service (for commercial customers with a delivery token)](https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/delivery-service/)

The simplified CSV (`targets.simple.csv`) and names-only plain text exports are discouraged: they flatten the entity graph and drop most of the data model. Use the FollowTheMoney JSON format instead.
